strengths: Fundamental Theoretical Discovery: The paper identifies and formalizes a widespread yet overlooked failure mode in modular diffusion steering: Marginal Path Collapse (MPC), where intermediate ratio-of-densities become non-normalizable even when terminal distributions are valid. The demonstration that finite score fields can mislead numerical solvers into transporting unintended paths (Example A.1) provides valuable conceptual clarity.

Sharp and Tractable Diagnostic: Theorem 2.1 provides a clean, necessary, and sufficient Path Existence Criterion (PEC) based on noise schedules and exponents for compactly supported distributions (and Gaussian mixtures in Appendix B.4). The criterion is easily verifiable analytically before running expensive inference.

Principled Methodological Extension: The proposed Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE) extends the Feynman–Kac steering framework to accommodate time-varying exponents $\gamma_i(t)$. The mathematical derivation using Itô's formula to track auxiliary log-density dynamics and particle importance weights is rigorous and complete.

Strong and Diverse Empirical Validation: The method is validated thoroughly across a controlled synthetic 2D benchmark, challenging 3D molecular generation tasks (flexible-pose scaffold decoration and fragment linking), and homogeneous compositional image generation (COCO-MIG). ACE consistently outperforms standard steering heuristics (NR) and existing Feynman–Kac correctors (FKC).

High Significance for AI for Science: Pretrained models in biology and chemistry (e.g., de novo generators, conformer models, and pocket-conditioned SBDD models) inherently employ distinct noise schedules and representations. Demonstrating how to soundly compose these heterogeneous models addresses a critical barrier in scientific applications.
weaknesses: Heuristic Choice of Bump Function Hyperparameters: While Theorem 2.2 guarantees the existence of valid bump functions, selecting the specific coefficients ($B_1, B_2$) relies on empirical tuning or manual prescreening. Although the paper provides sensitivity analysis showing a stable range, an automated or optimal criterion-guided schedule optimization would make the framework more seamless.

Computational Overhead of Full Particle Tracking: Tracking component log-densities and computing vector field divergences (or Hutchinson trace estimators) along with particle resampling increases inference latency and memory compared to naive CFG-style heuristics. While ACE-lite is proposed to skip resampling, it loses some of the worst-case sample quality guarantees.

Boundary Singularity Handling: Because noise schedules satisfy $\alpha_1 = 0$, the criterion $C(t)$ diverges or exhibits singular behavior as $t \to 1$. The framework relies on truncating integration at $t_{\text{end}} < 1$ (e.g., $0.999$) followed by a single Euler step, which, while standard in diffusion literature, leaves the very endpoint boundary behavior dependent on a discretization heuristic.

strengths: Identification of a fundamental and practically relevant failure mode: The paper discovers and formalizes 'Marginal Path Collapse' (MPC) in ratio-of-densities diffusion steering, explaining why naive composition of heterogeneous experts (with differing noise schedules or negative exponents) causes the intermediate density to become non-normalizable even when endpoint densities are well-behaved.

Rigor and depth of theoretical results: Theorem 2.1 provides a clean, sharp, and verifiable Path Existence Criterion (PEC) based on noise schedules and exponent weights for compactly supported targets. The paper also derives necessary and sufficient conditions for Gaussian Mixture targets (Theorem B.3) and connects PEC magnitude to intermediate distribution concentration via quantile radius bounds (Proposition 2.1 / E.1).

Principled generalization of Feynman–Kac steering: The authors successfully extend Feynman–Kac diffusion steering to time-varying exponent schedules (Theorem 2.3 / A.1), formally accounting for the distributional time-drift term via tracked auxiliary log-density dynamics.

Compelling and diverse empirical validation: Experiments span controlled synthetic 2D benchmarks, realistic high-dimensional molecular design tasks (flexible-pose scaffold decoration and fragment linking on CrossDocked2020), and compositional text-to-image generation (COCO-MIG). In regimes where path collapse occurs, ACE consistently restores sampling validity and outperforms uncorrected baselines (NR, FKC).

Thorough contextualization and ablation: The paper includes a systematic survey of noise schedules across existing molecular diffusion literature (Tables E.7–E.9) proving that schedule heterogeneity is a genuine practical bottleneck, along with extensive sensitivity analyses on bump parameters and ESS thresholds.
weaknesses: Computational overhead of particle weighting and resampling: Simulating the weighted SDE with auxiliary log-density tracking and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) resampling increases runtime and memory overhead compared to heuristic score mixing. While ACE-lite is introduced to bypass resampling, it sacrifices the theoretical unbiasedness of the particle system.

Heuristic specification of bump parameters: Although the criterion C(t) > 0 is analytical, the choice of bump function parameters (B1, B2) remains somewhat empirical; overly aggressive bumps can act as score multipliers and amplify network approximation errors, as discussed in the sensitivity analysis.

Scope of theoretical guarantees: The main Path Existence Criterion (Theorem 2.1) relies on the assumption of compactly supported data targets. While applicable to bounded domains such as images and centered molecular coordinates, extension to unconstrained continuous domains with heavy tails remains unaddressed.

strengths: Identification of a fundamental pathology: The paper clearly identifies and formalizes Marginal Path Collapse (MPC), showing that composing heterogeneous generative experts with mismatched schedules and negative exponents frequently produces non-integrable intermediate densities, even when endpoints are valid.

Rigorous theoretical foundation: The Path Existence Criterion (Theorem 2.1 / B.1) provides sharp necessary and sufficient conditions for compactly supported targets (and Gaussian mixture models in Theorem B.3). Furthermore, the concentration bound (Proposition 2.1 / E.1) neatly links the criterion value C(t) to the effective variance/quantile radius of intermediate distributions.

Principled generalization of Feynman–Kac steering: Extending FKC to time-varying exponent schedules (Theorem 2.3 / A.1) by tracking component log-densities via auxiliary Itô dynamics is theoretically elegant and resolves the validity violation without requiring retraining.

Comprehensive empirical validation across diverse domains: The method is validated on synthetic 2D benchmarks, flexible-pose scaffold decoration on CrossDocked2020, fragment linking, and compositional text-to-image generation on COCO-MIG, consistently demonstrating the necessity of path correction under high guidance scales.

Extensive analysis of scheduler prevalence: The survey and quantitative analysis across 125 schedule combinations in the appendix convincingly establish that heterogeneous scheduling is standard and that MPC is an inherent practical challenge rather than a contrived edge case.
weaknesses: Heuristic selection of bump parameters: While Theorem 2.2 constructively proves the existence of a corrective bump function, determining the specific amplitude parameters (B1, B2) currently requires empirical tuning or manual pre-screening to balance path existence against the amplification of score estimation errors.

Computational overhead of exact ACE: Simulating the auxiliary log-density dynamics and performing particle resampling increases runtime and memory usage relative to standard heuristic guidance (e.g., NR). Although ACE-lite mitigates this overhead, it reintroduces variance and discards the formal Feynman–Kac sampling guarantees.

Restriction to continuous spatial representations: The current formulation relies on stochastic interpolants over continuous variables (e.g., 3D coordinates). In molecular tasks, discrete and categorical features (such as atom types and formal charges) require post-hoc heuristic handling or continuous one-hot relaxations, limiting end-to-end applicability in mixed continuous-discrete spaces.
